title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows, improve cache parallelism and deps hygiene
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: our GitHub Actions workflows have accumulated multiple overlapping lint/test/release pipelines which increase matrix runtime, duplicate cache computations, and make dependency hygiene noisy for contributors. This PR consolidates the lint/test/release workflows into a smaller set of purpose-driven workflows, standardizes cache keys and parallelism for node/python matrices, and upgrades a few housekeeping dev-dependencies to reduce noisy alerts. Goals: reduce CI median runtime, improve cache hit-rate, simplify developer mental model for PR hygiene, and decrease intermittent flakiness in release automation. Changes: 1) Consolidated 6 workflows into 3: .github/workflows/lint.yml (all repos and SDKs), .github/workflows/test.yml (matrix + targeted integration lanes), and .github/workflows/release.yml (release automation + changelog validation). 2) Introduced cache key refactor: repo-level cache with job-scoped fallback and deterministic restore order to improve parallelism and reduce lock contention. 3) Reduced matrix permutations by splitting fast/slow test lanes and using conditional job execution for affected packages only. 4) Upgraded GitHub Actions runner images and bumped several dev-deps in JS/TS toolchain (eslint 9.x -> 9.8, typescript 5.5 -> 5.6) and pinned node versions to Node 20 in CI. 5) Added lightweight preflight job that runs quick static checks and exits early for docs-only changes. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflows and validate syntax - [x] Add deterministic cache keys and fallback order - [x] Keep per-repo overrides for SDK packages - [x] Update docs/CONTRIBUTING.md CI section - [x] Run canary CI on redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-python sample repos - [x] Address reviewer feedback and re-run failing matrix lanes How this was validated: ran full workflow on fork and internal canaries, measured runtime improvements (~25% median reduction across lint+unit), observed higher cache hits for node modules across repeated runs, and validated release job still creates draft release and changelog entries in dry-run mode. Rollout plan: merge to main and monitor GitHub Actions metrics for 72 hours; keep rollback branch ready in case of regressions. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps a small set of path filters to avoid running heavy integration lanes for doc/README changes. If regressions are noticed we can further split slow lanes and add per-repo opt-ins.
commits: 6 commits: 1) chore(ci): add consolidated workflows and path filters; 2) feat(ci): implement deterministic cache key and fallback; 3) perf(ci): split test matrix into fast/slow lanes; 4) deps: bump eslint/typescript, pin node 20 in runners; 5) docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md CI section; 6) fix(ci): adjust job name/outputs after reviewer feedback
review_comments: Miguel Ramos (reviewer): Can we avoid adding a global cache key that invalidates too often? Please make sure package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml are included. Author: added deterministic hash order and included lockfile in key.

Priya Patel (reviewer): The release workflow change looks good, but please keep a dry-run toggle and test against the staging release repo. Author: added env RELEASE_DRY_RUN=true by default and ran canary.

Samir Dutta (reviewer): The matrix split is smart but ensure that tests for redwood-private-installer still run in slow lane. Author: added path-based override to force slow lane for private-installer.
CI bot: unit-tests (linux) failed on first run due to race in canary teardown. Author: fixed teardown ordering in scripts/ci/preflight.sh and re-ran. CI bot: all checks green on final run.
Miguel Ramos: Approved after CI green and docs updated.
Priya Patel: Approved - minor nit on cache docs resolved.
merge_outcome: merged via squash and merge by Miguel Ramos after 2 approvals and CI green
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows to reduce duplication and improve cache parallelism; bumped dev dependencies (eslint, typescript) and pinned Node 20 for CI runners; added preflight static checks and deterministic cache keys to improve cache hit rate and reduce flaky runs.
notes_short: 25% median CI runtime reduction observed in canary runs; monitor first 72 hours post-merge for regressions.
